name: Tripwire

method.history: daily closes: Yahoo chart (10y, adjusted where Yahoo provides it) for 25 markets incl. crypto in AUD, plus the 5 leveraged funds the high-yield sleeve holds; ECB/Frankfurter for the 6 FX pairs
method.rebalance: monthly, first trading day, close to close, through a 2pp no-trade band per leg
method.lookahead: signal at close t, weights govern returns from t+1
method.costs: per unit turnover: 25bps crypto, 20bps leveraged ETFs, 10bps stocks/indices/metals/energy, 3bps FX
method.leverage: held inside the instrument (2x/3x daily-reset ETFs), so financing and daily-rebalance drag are in the price series, not in a made-up weight above 1
method.warmup: 273 daily closes before a market is eligible (200d MA + 12-1 momentum)

tiers.name: Digest

algo.name: Gauge
rules: Hold every market with 273 daily closes, equal weight — 1/31 each once all 31 are live.
Long while breadth (% of those markets above their 200-day average) is at least 55%; exit below 45% — a band, not a cliff.
Between the two: hold what you hold. Below 45% breadth: cash. No shorts, no leverage, at most one switch a month.
Rebalance the first trading day of each month, and only through a 2-point no-trade band; 10bps per unit of turnover (25 crypto, 3 FX).
algo.honest: The free tier arms nothing and mails nothing, so this is the engine on paper: the same switch the paid tiers use, watchable for nobody's money.

stacks.name: Momentum
stacks.what: Own a leg while it is above its 200-day average with positive 12-1 momentum; size 1/vol, 40% cap.
stacks.wins: long, one-way trends — 2020-21, 2023-24
stacks.loses: whipsaw: a market that crosses its average six times a year pays six round trips

stacks.name: Trend & breakout
stacks.what: Own a leg only while it is above both its 200-day and its 50-day average and closing at a 63-day high; equal weight, so the few names that qualify carry the book.
stacks.wins: breakouts that keep going, and quiet starts to big moves
stacks.loses: a market grinding sideways just under its high — the entry is always a little late and the exit a little early

stacks.name: Mean reversion
stacks.what: Own a leg while it is above its 200-day average but below its 20-day average (a pullback inside an uptrend), sized by depth of the dip over its own volatility.
stacks.wins: choppy bull markets where every dip gets bought
stacks.loses: a real trend change: the 200-day average turns last, so the first three dips are the whole drawdown

stacks.name: Low volatility
stacks.what: Of the legs above their 200-day average, keep the calmest half by 63-day volatility; 1/vol inside that half.
stacks.wins: risk-off years, and any client who measures the ride and not only the return
stacks.loses: a melt-up led by the loudest names — this style is structurally underweight what runs

stacks.name: Risk parity
stacks.what: Own every leg above its 200-day average, with no momentum filter at all, and split the risk 1/vol — one leg per cluster where the tier has clusters.
stacks.wins: broad participation: the least opinionated way to be invested
stacks.loses: a market that is above its average and falling — it holds the leg the other four styles have already sold

tiers.verdict: profitable net of costs out of sample (+9.64% a year) but behind its own baseline (+11.64%)

tiers.name: Tripwire

algo.name: Band
rules: Universe is the 4 markets a subscriber arms first: BTC, ETH, SOL, AUD/USD — any 4 of the 31.
A leg is held while it is above its 200-day average and its 12-1 momentum is positive; otherwise that leg is cash.
Held legs are sized 1/volatility (63-day, annualised) with a 40% cap each; the rest is cash.
Rebalance monthly through the 2-point band; the tripwire is the exit you already have, so the algorithm needs no stop it cannot see.
algo.honest: The band tells you when you were wrong; the trend tells you when you were right. Arithmetic, not a forecast.

tiers.name: Package

algo.name: Scale
rules: Weights stay exactly as published — the basket is rebalanced back to them, never re-shaped.
Each basket's exposure is 1, 0.5 or 0, read off its own index vs its 200-day average and 12-1 momentum.
Capital is split equally across the three baskets; whatever a scale leaves unspent is cash at 0%.
A 10% portfolio drawdown halves every exposure until equity recovers to within 5% of the peak.
algo.honest: Weights are the only opinion in the file; the algorithm only decides how much of the basket to own — the smallest opinion on top of the one you already bought.

tiers.name: Package · high yield

algo.name: Gear
rules: One sleeve over both kinds of market: the owned ones (BTC, ETH, WTI crude) and the bought leverage (S&P 500 3x, Nasdaq-100 3x, semis 3x, 20y Treasuries 3x, gold 2x) — eight instruments in five clusters: US index leverage, Treasuries, gold, crypto, crude.
The leverage is a holding, not a weight above 1: a 3x fund's price already carries its financing and its daily rebalance, so the drag is measured instead of promised.

A leg is bought only while it is above its own 200-day average with positive 12-1 momentum; inside a cluster only the strongest momentum leg is held, so three 3x equity funds are one position and a choice — never three bets.

The risk budget is split 1/vol across the clusters that are in, capped at 40% a leg, then the sleeve is scaled so its ex-ante vol is the tier's target — 15% core, 22% balanced, 30% high yield; a 20% drawdown halves the sleeve until equity is back within 6% of the peak.
Monthly rebalance through the 2-point band, 20bps per unit of turnover on a levered fund, 25bps crypto, 10bps crude; cash earns 0% and an empty sleeve holds cash.
algo.honest: This is the tier where the arithmetic can hurt: a 3x fund that halves needs to double just to be even, and a 30% vol target means one month in twenty is a bad one. The vol target is a dial, not a floor — the sleeve is often less than fully invested.
